# AI Provider & Inference Infrastructure Checklist: AI Provider & Local Inference Foundation

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality (completeness, clarity, consistency,
measurability, coverage) of the AI provider/inference-infrastructure requirements —
readiness lifecycle, request queuing/concurrency, timeout handling, error taxonomy, and
accelerator fallback — before proceeding to `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-08-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on
feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review
artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality
criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for
requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the exact set of readiness lifecycle states (not-loaded/loading/ready/unavailable) and their permitted transitions fully enumerated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for what triggers a transition back to "not-loaded" from another state, or is that transition explicitly disallowed? [Gap]
- [x] CHK003 Is the maximum queue depth (or explicit absence of a limit) for serialized inference requests specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for what happens to already-queued requests if the model transitions to "unavailable" while they are waiting? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK005 Is the default timeout value and its unit specified as a requirement, or only implied by design notes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for whether a per-request timeout override has upper/lower bounds? [Gap]
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements defined for how the "visible notice" of accelerator fallback is surfaced to a caller, versus left unspecified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is "actionable reason" (Spec §User Story 2, FR-004) defined with any criteria for what makes a reason actionable, or left to interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK009 Is "distinguishable, actionable error conditions" (FR-010) quantified via a closed set of categories rather than left as a general adjective? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK010 Is "configurable" (FR-003 cache/model location, FR-017 timeout) defined in terms of who configures it and when (startup-only vs. runtime-adjustable)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003, FR-017]
- [x] CHK011 Is "processing another request" (the busy condition in FR-018) precisely scoped to a single in-flight inference call, or could it also include the queue-wait period itself? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-018]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK012 Do the "no automatic retry" requirement (FR-019) and the "queue and process serially" requirement (FR-018) agree on what happens to requests queued behind one whose load attempt fails? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, FR-019]
- [x] CHK013 Do the readiness-state requirements (FR-004) and the accelerator-fallback requirement (FR-008) agree on whether an active-but-degraded (CPU-fallback) provider is reported as "ready" or as a distinct state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, FR-008]
- [x] CHK014 Are the "no automatic cloud fallback" requirement (FR-007) and the "automatic CPU fallback" requirement (FR-008) clearly distinguished so the two different "automatic fallback" behaviors cannot be confused? [Clarity/Consistency, Spec §FR-007, FR-008]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK015 Can SC-007 ("under 5 seconds... without inspecting logs or code") be objectively verified given the current requirements, or does it need a defined measurement method? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [x] CHK016 Is SC-005 ("100% of local-inference failure scenarios exercised during testing") paired with a defined, enumerable list of failure scenarios, or is the set left open-ended? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK017 Are acceptance criteria defined for confirming the queue processes requests in the order received (FIFO), or only that they are serialized? [Gap, Spec §FR-018]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a second model-load failure occurring after a user has already taken the explicit retry action from a prior failure (FR-019)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for an inference request timing out while the model is also concurrently transitioning to "unavailable"? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the readiness state reported while accelerator fallback (FR-008) is actively in progress, or only the before/after states? [Coverage, Gap]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Does the spec define behavior when the configured timeout is shorter than the time required just to load the model (as opposed to run inference)? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK022 Is the interaction between "insufficient disk space" (Edge Cases) and "no automatic retry" (FR-019) explicitly addressed — i.e., does freeing space still require an explicit retry? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-019]
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for what a caller receives when local-only mode is enabled but no model has ever been provisioned (readiness "not-loaded" with no load ever attempted)? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK024 Are resource-consumption limits (e.g., maximum queued requests, memory bound) specified as non-functional requirements, or left entirely unbounded? [Gap, NFR]
- [x] CHK025 Are logging/observability requirements for the queue and readiness state machine specified with enough precision to be implemented consistently across the codebase? [Clarity, Plan §Research #10]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Is the assumption that CPU inference is always available as a fallback target (i.e., never itself unavailable) explicitly documented and validated? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements dependent on hardware/OS-level accelerator detection capability documented as an external dependency with its own failure mode? [Dependency, Gap]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK028 Is there a single, unambiguous requirement stating whether the timeout clock starts at enqueue time or at start-of-inference time? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017, FR-018]
- [x] CHK029 Is it unambiguous whether "unavailable" (FR-004) is reserved for permanent/blocking failures only, or also used transiently during a retry-eligible failure window? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, FR-019]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
